header: Reference notes for you only. Use them so the answer is accurate and consistent with the learner's material, but answer the question above directly and never mention these notes:

blocks.general:
General facts (all exams):
- CEFR levels: A2 = basic user (everyday routines, simple exchanges), B1 = independent user (main points
  of clear standard speech, connected text on familiar topics, describe experiences and plans, give
  reasons), B2 = can follow complex texts, discuss abstractly, write clear detailed texts and argue a view.
- C1 = proficient user: speaks spontaneously and fluently, knows colloquial idioms and can vary the style
  deliberately, keeps a high degree of grammatical accuracy (telc's description), communicates in complex
  social and professional contexts with a high degree of correctness and appropriateness (ÖSD's description).
  C2 = understands practically everything read or heard with ease, summarises information from several
  written and spoken sources with reasons and explanations, expresses itself spontaneously, very fluently
  and precisely and brings out finer shades of meaning (Goethe-Institut's description).
- Goethe-Institut recommends roughly 200-350 lessons (45 min) before A2, 350-650 before B1, 600-800
  before B2, 800-1,000 before C1 and at least 1,000 before C2; the actual need depends on the learner.
- Official free practice: the Goethe-Institut publishes "Modellsatz" and "Übungssatz" sets for each level on
  goethe.de (with audio and answer keys); telc publishes "Übungstest" PDFs with audio on telc.net; the BAMF
  and telc publish DTZ Modelltests. Always practise with the current versions of these.
- Certificates do not formally expire, but universities, employers and immigration authorities often ask for
  a certificate that is not older than 1-2 years; check the requirement of the institution.
- Prices are set by the test centre; in Germany a B1 exam is typically in the range of about 150-300 EUR,
  B2 somewhat more. Registration deadlines are usually several weeks before the date.
- Recognised for German citizenship (Einbürgerung: level B1) and settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis:
  usually B1) are among others the Goethe-Zertifikat, telc Deutsch, ÖSD and the DTZ; check the current rules
  of the responsible office, they change.
- Register: learners must not mix "du" and "Sie" inside one letter; formal letters use "Sehr geehrte Damen
  und Herren," / "Sehr geehrte Frau X," and close with "Mit freundlichen Grüßen" (no comma after the closing,
  name on the next line); informal letters use "Liebe Anna," / "Lieber Tom," and "Liebe Grüße" or "Viele Grüße".
  After the comma of the salutation the first word is written in lower case unless it is a noun or "Sie".
- ÖSD (Österreichisches Sprachdiplom Deutsch) is a separate provider - not Goethe and not telc: a
  state-recognised Austrian exam system run by an independent non-profit association, with exams from the
  ÖSD Zertifikat A1 up to the ÖSD Zertifikat C1 and ÖSD Zertifikat C2 (plus youth and job-specific versions).
  Austrian universities accept ÖSD certificates between B1 and C2 - which level depends on the university and
  the programme - as the language proof for admission to German-language degrees (and ask for A2 already at
  application since the 2019 summer semester); German universities accept the ÖSD Zertifikat B2, C1 or C2
  depending on the university, and under the HRK/KMK Rahmenordnung (RO-DT § 8) the ÖSD Zertifikat C2 exempts
  from the DSH/TestDaF requirement. Above B2 the choice is therefore Goethe C1/C2, telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule,
  TestDaF, DSH or ÖSD C1/C2 - pick by what the target institution lists.
blocks.goethe-a2:
Goethe-Zertifikat A2 (format since 2016):
- One exam with four parts, 100 points in total: Lesen 25 points, Hören 25, Schreiben 25, Sprechen 25.
- Pass rule: at least 60 points overall, and within that at least 45 of the 75 written points (Lesen +
  Hören + Schreiben together) and at least 15 of the 25 speaking points.
- Lesen: 30 minutes, 4 Teile, 20 items (short everyday texts: newspaper notice, e-mails/messages, ads,
  notices/signs; item types: multiple choice and matching).
- Hören: about 30 minutes, 4 Teile, 20 items (short announcements/radio messages, a conversation, short
  monologues; most parts are played twice).
- Schreiben: 30 minutes, 2 Aufgaben: Teil 1 a short private message (SMS/chat/e-mail to a friend, about
  20-30 words, three content points given); Teil 2 a somewhat more formal e-mail/letter (about 30-40 words,
  three content points given).
- Sprechen: about 15 minutes for two candidates, 3 Teile: Teil 1 ask and answer questions about the person
  using keyword cards (e.g. "Hobby?", "Arbeit?"); Teil 2 talk about yourself on a topic card with four
  keywords (e.g. "Wohnen: Wo? Mit wem? Seit wann? Wie?"); Teil 3 plan something together (e.g. agree on a
  time and place to meet) as a dialogue.
- Grades (out of 100): 100-90 sehr gut, 89-80 gut, 79-70 befriedigend, 69-60 ausreichend, below 60 nicht
  bestanden.
blocks.goethe-b1:
Goethe-Zertifikat B1 (developed jointly by Goethe-Institut, ÖSD and Universität Freiburg/CH, since 2013):
- Modular exam: four independent modules Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen. Each module has 100 points and
  is passed with at least 60 points. Modules can be taken together or separately; a passed module is
  certified on its own, and only a failed module has to be repeated. Grades per module: 100-90 sehr gut,
  89-80 gut, 79-70 befriedigend, 69-60 ausreichend, below 60 nicht bestanden.
- Lesen: 65 minutes, 5 Teile, 30 items. Teil 1: a blog/diary-style text, 6 richtig/falsch items. Teil 2:
  two short press texts, 6 multiple-choice items (3 options). Teil 3: match 7 people/situations to 10
  advertisements (some get "kein passendes Angebot"). Teil 4: 7 readers' comments on a controversial
  question, decide for each whether the author is for (ja) or against (nein). Teil 5: an instruction
  text or house rules, 4 multiple-choice items. Answers go on the Antwortbogen.
- Hören: about 40 minutes, 4 Teile, 30 items. Teil 1: 5 short texts (announcements, messages), each
  played twice, 10 items (per text one richtig/falsch and one multiple choice). Teil 2: a longer
  monologue such as a guided tour or a talk, played once, 5 multiple-choice items. Teil 3: an everyday
  conversation, played once, 7 richtig/falsch items. Teil 4: a radio discussion with a moderator and two
  guests, played twice, 8 items ("who says what").
- Schreiben: 60 minutes, 3 Aufgaben, 100 points. Aufgabe 1 (about 20 minutes, 40 points): informal e-mail
  to a friend on three given content points, about 80 words. Aufgabe 2 (about 25 minutes, 40 points):
  a written opinion for a forum or a readers' letter on a topic, about 80 words, with a short summary of
  the issue, your own view with reasons and an example. Aufgabe 3 (about 15 minutes, 20 points): a short
  formal or semi-formal message (e.g. cancel a meeting, apologise, ask for information) to a teacher,
  boss or office, about 40 words. Each Aufgabe is rated on four criteria: Erfüllung (task and content
  points), Kohärenz (structure, connectors), Wortschatz, Strukturen (grammar), on a scale from A (best)
  to E; an answer that misses the topic or is clearly too short loses most of its points.
- Sprechen: about 15 minutes for two candidates (with an examiner pair), 15 minutes preparation time
  beforehand, 3 Teile, 100 points. Teil 1 "Gemeinsam etwas planen" (about 3 minutes, 28 points): plan
  something together as a dialogue from a task card with points to discuss (e.g. a party, a trip, a
  visit). Teil 2 "Ein Thema präsentieren" (about 3 minutes per candidate, 40 points): a short
  presentation following five given slides ("Folien"): 1 introduce the topic, 2 your personal
  experience, 3 the situation in your home country, 4 advantages and disadvantages plus your opinion,
  5 closing and thanks. Teil 3 "Über ein Thema sprechen" (about 2 minutes per candidate, 16 points):
  give feedback on the partner's presentation and ask a question, and answer the partner's and the
  examiner's question about your own presentation. Aussprache (pronunciation) is rated separately with
  16 points. Criteria: Erfüllung/Interaktion, Wortschatz, Strukturen, Aussprache.
blocks.goethe-b2:
Goethe-Zertifikat B2 (new format since 2019, for adults and for young people):
- Modular like B1: Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen, 100 points each, 60 points pass each module,
  modules can be taken separately and a passed module does not have to be repeated. Same grade bands as B1.
- Lesen: 65 minutes, 5 Teile, 30 items: opinions of several people on a topic in a forum ("who says
  what"), a press article with multiple choice, a text with removed sentences to put back, matching
  short comments/statements to headings or people, and an instruction or rules text with multiple
  choice. Texts are longer and more abstract than at B1.
- Hören: about 40 minutes, 4 Teile, 30 items: several short everyday texts, a radio interview or report,
  a conversation between several people ("who says what"), and a talk or lecture with multiple choice;
  some parts are played twice, others only once.
- Schreiben: 75 minutes, 2 Aufgaben. Aufgabe 1 (about 50 minutes, weighted more heavily): a discussion
  contribution for an online forum on a given topic with guiding points, at least 150 words. Aufgabe 2
  (about 25 minutes): a formal or semi-formal message, e.g. to a colleague, boss or teacher, at least
  100 words, on given content points. Criteria: task fulfilment/content, coherence, vocabulary, grammar.
- Sprechen: about 15 minutes for two candidates, 15 minutes preparation, 2 Teile. Teil 1 "Vortrag": a
  short talk (about 4 minutes) on one of two offered topics, structured as introduction, several
  options/alternatives, advantages and disadvantages, your opinion, conclusion; afterwards the partner
  and the examiner ask questions. Teil 2 "Diskussion": both candidates discuss a controversial statement
  (about 5 minutes), give arguments, react to the other, and reach a conclusion.
blocks.telc-b1:
telc Deutsch B1 (also called "Zertifikat Deutsch"; sister versions telc Deutsch B1 Schule, telc Deutsch B1+
Beruf; the DTZ is a separate scaled A2/B1 exam):
- One exam with a written part (225 points) and an oral part (75 points), 300 points in total. Pass rule:
  at least 60 % in the written part (135 points) AND at least 60 % in the oral part (45 points). Grades by
  total: 300-270 sehr gut, 269.5-240 gut, 239.5-210 befriedigend, 209.5-180 ausreichend. A failed part
  (written or oral) can usually be repeated on its own within one year; ask the test centre.
- Leseverstehen + Sprachbausteine: 90 minutes together (you divide the time yourself). Leseverstehen: 3
  Teile, 20 items, 75 points: Teil 1 Globalverstehen (match 5 short texts to 10 headlines), Teil 2
  Detailverstehen (a longer text, 5 multiple-choice items), Teil 3 Selektives Verstehen (match 10
  situations to 12 advertisements; for some the answer is "x" = no suitable ad). Sprachbausteine: 2
  Teile, 20 items, 30 points: Teil 1 a letter with 10 gaps, three options (a/b/c) for each gap, mostly
  grammar (connectors, prepositions, pronouns, verb forms, adjective endings); Teil 2 a text with 10 gaps
  to fill from a bank of 15 words (a-o), five words remain unused.
- Hörverstehen: about 30 minutes, 3 Teile, 20 items, 75 points: Teil 1 Globalverstehen (5 short texts,
  richtig/falsch, played once), Teil 2 Detailverstehen (an interview or report, 10 richtig/falsch
  items, played once), Teil 3 Selektives Verstehen (5 short announcements, richtig/falsch, played twice).
- Schriftlicher Ausdruck: 30 minutes, 45 points: one semi-formal or formal letter/e-mail replying to a
  given text (an advertisement, a letter, a notice) with FOUR Leitpunkte that all have to be addressed;
  about 100 words is a sensible length, there is no strict word limit. Rated on three criteria of 15
  points each: I Berücksichtigung der Leitpunkte (all four points covered appropriately), II
  Kommunikative Gestaltung (register, salutation and closing, structure, connectors), III Formale
  Richtigkeit (grammar, spelling, punctuation). Missing a Leitpunkt costs heavily in criterion I.
- Mündlicher Ausdruck: about 15 minutes for two candidates after 20 minutes of preparation (notes
  allowed), 3 Teile, 75 points: Teil 1 Kontaktaufnahme (15 points): get to know your partner - name,
  origin, family, work or studies, languages, free time, plans. Teil 2 Gespräch über ein Thema (30
  points): each candidate gets a short text or statistic on a topic, tells the partner what it says,
  then both exchange experiences and opinions. Teil 3 Gemeinsam eine Aufgabe lösen (30 points): plan or
  organise something together (e.g. a farewell party, a trip, a visit) and agree on details.
blocks.telc-b2:
telc Deutsch B2:
- Same architecture as telc B1 with harder tasks: written part 225 points (Leseverstehen 75,
  Sprachbausteine 30, Hörverstehen 75, Schriftlicher Ausdruck 45), oral part 75, total 300; pass with
  at least 60 % in the written part AND 60 % in the oral part; same grade bands (180 ausreichend, 210
  befriedigend, 240 gut, 270 sehr gut).
- Leseverstehen + Sprachbausteine: 90 minutes; Leseverstehen 3 Teile, 20 items (headline matching,
  detailed multiple choice on a longer text, matching situations to ads); Sprachbausteine 2 Teile, 20
  items (10 multiple-choice gaps, 10 gaps from a 15-word bank) testing B2 grammar such as Konjunktiv II,
  Passiv, Partizipialattribute, two-part connectors, verbs with prepositions, nominal style.
- Hörverstehen: about 20 minutes, 3 Teile, 20 items (global, detailed, selective listening; longer
  interviews or reports, most played once).
- Schriftlicher Ausdruck: 30 minutes, 45 points: choose ONE of two tasks (A or B) and write a formal or
  semi-formal letter/e-mail (complaint, application, request, statement) on given points; aim for
  roughly 150 words or more; criteria I content/task, II communicative design, III formal correctness,
  15 points each.
- Mündlicher Ausdruck: about 15 minutes for two candidates after 20 minutes preparation, 3 Teile:
  Teil 1 Präsentation (each candidate presents a topic for about 1.5 minutes, the partner asks
  questions), Teil 2 Diskussion (discuss a statement or text with arguments and counter-arguments),
  Teil 3 Problemlösung (plan or decide something together).
blocks.dtz:
Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer (DTZ, A2-B1), the final exam of the integration course (Integrationskurs),
developed by telc for the BAMF:
- A scaled exam: the certificate reports a level per area - Hören/Lesen (one area), Schreiben, Sprechen -
  each as B1, A2 or "unter A2". Overall result B1 requires B1 in Sprechen AND B1 in at least one of the
  two other areas (Hören/Lesen or Schreiben); the remaining area may be A2. Without B1 in Sprechen the
  overall result cannot be B1.
- Written part about 100 minutes: Hören about 25 minutes, 4 Teile (announcements, radio/phone messages,
  everyday conversations, opinions of several people); Lesen 45 minutes, 5 Teile (notices, ads, a
  press text, a formal letter/official text, opinions); item types are multiple choice, matching and
  richtig/falsch. Schreiben 30 minutes: choose ONE of two tasks and write a semi-formal or formal letter
  or e-mail (e.g. to a Kita, landlord, employer, office, school) covering all the given Leitpunkte
  (usually three or four), with salutation, introduction, the points, request, closing and greeting.
- Sprechen: about 16 minutes for two candidates, 3 Teile: Teil 1 "Über sich sprechen" (1A introduce
  yourself with keywords such as name, origin, family, work, languages; 1B answer the examiner's
  follow-up questions); Teil 2 "Über Erfahrungen sprechen" (2A describe a picture: where, who, what,
  what you think; 2B talk about your own experiences with the topic and ask your partner); Teil 3
  "Gemeinsam etwas planen" (organise something together from a task card, e.g. a joint outing, a
  present, a course).
- Purpose: B1 in the DTZ is the usual language proof for the settlement permit and for naturalisation
  (together with the "Leben in Deutschland" test from the Orientierungskurs). Course participants take
  the DTZ free of charge at the end of their course; the exam can be repeated.
blocks.goethe-c1:
Goethe-Zertifikat C1 (new modular format; Durchführungsbestimmungen of 1 September 2023, applied to exams after
1 January 2024):
- Four independent modules Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen, taken individually or in combination. The three
  written modules are a group exam; Sprechen is normally a pair exam (an individual exam only in exceptional
  cases). Offered in digital format (at the centre) or on paper, with the same standards worldwide.
- Each module has a maximum of 100 points = 100 % and is passed with at least 60 points (60 %). Prädikate per
  module: 100-90 sehr gut, 89-80 gut, 79-70 befriedigend, 69-60 ausreichend, 59-0 nicht bestanden. Modules
  can be taken and repeated as often as desired, as far as the centre's capacity allows.
- Lesen: 65 minutes, Teil 1-4, 30 items (forum posts, newspaper and magazine articles, commentaries,
  instructions; key information, details, viewpoints, opinions and rules). Each item scores 1 or 0; the
  checkpoints are multiplied by 3.33 and rounded to give the score out of 100 (18 of 30 = 60 = pass). Plan
  about 5 minutes within the exam time for transferring the answers to the Antwortbogen.
- Hören: about 40 minutes, Teil 1-4, 30 items (interviews, presentations, conversations, everyday remarks,
  radio broadcasts; main points and key details), scored like Lesen (x 3.33); about 3 minutes within the
  time for the Antwortbogen.
- Schreiben: 75 minutes, Teil 1-2: a forum post in which you express and justify your opinion on a current
  social theme, and a formal message in a professional context. Maximum 100 points; two raters score
  independently and the arithmetic mean is rounded to whole points; a third rating is made when one rater
  is below and one above 60 and the mean is below 60.
- Sprechen: Teil 1-2, about 20 minutes as a pair (about 15 minutes as an individual exam) plus 20 minutes of
  preparation time (notes on stamped paper allowed). A short introduction of about one minute (not graded);
  Teil 1: each candidate gives a short Vortrag on one of two topics offered, about 7 minutes per candidate
  including the questions of the partner and an examiner; Teil 2: both candidates discuss a controversial
  topic together, about 5 minutes for both. Two examiners rate independently; maximum 100 points.
- The written modules take about 180 minutes without breaks; recommended order Lesen - Hören - Schreiben
  with a break of at least 15 minutes between modules.
- Target group: adults; a minimum age of 16 is recommended; the Goethe-Institut estimates 800-1,000 teaching
  units of 45 minutes to reach C1, depending on previous knowledge.
blocks.goethe-c2:
Goethe-Zertifikat C2: Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom (GDS; Durchführungsbestimmungen of 1 September 2025):
- Four independent modules Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen, taken individually or in combination; the three
  written modules are a group exam, Sprechen is an individual exam (Einzelprüfung). Four module certificates
  equal one overall certificate. The literature-based Schreiben tasks are created together with the
  Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München.
- Each module: maximum 100 points = 100 %, passed with at least 60 points (60 %); Prädikate 100-90 sehr gut,
  89-80 gut, 79-70 befriedigend, 69-60 ausreichend, 59-0 nicht bestanden. Modules can be repeated as often as
  desired, capacity permitting.
- Lesen: 80 minutes, Teil 1-4 (Sachtexte, Kommentare, Reportagen, Anzeigen - abstract and linguistically
  complex texts including implicit meaning); 1 or 0 points per answer, the parts are added up to a maximum of
  100. About 5 minutes within the time for the Antwortbogen.
- Hören: about 35 minutes, Teil 1-3 (reports and Reportagen from the media, informal conversations, expert
  interviews at natural speed); 1 or 0 points per answer, maximum 100; 3 minutes for the Antwortbogen.
- Schreiben: 80 minutes, Teil 1-2. Teil 1: rephrase parts of a Kurzreferat - 10 answers scored 2, 1 or 0 =
  maximum 20 points. Teil 2: one well-structured text (Leserbrief or Buchrezension) on ONE of four topics -
  two general topics and two literature-based topics (one per book on the year's Literaturliste, which is
  published online and valid for the calendar year); five criteria scored 4-0 = 20 points, multiplied by
  four = maximum 80 points.
- Sprechen: about 15 minutes plus 15 minutes of preparation; an introduction of about 2-3 minutes (not
  graded); Teil 1 Produktion: a free Vortrag of about 5 minutes on the topic chosen from two (e.g.
  globalisation), followed by about 2-3 minutes of questions; Teil 2 Interaktion: about 5 minutes - choose
  one of two topics and the Pro or Contra side, open the discussion, and the second examiner argues the other
  side. Two examiners rate independently; the points of Teil 1 and 2 are added and multiplied by 2.5 to give
  the score out of 100.
- The written modules take about 195 minutes without breaks; recommended order Lesen - Hören - Schreiben
  with breaks of at least 15 minutes.
- Target group: adults; a minimum age of 18 is recommended; the Goethe-Institut estimates at least 1,000
  teaching units of 45 minutes to reach C2. On 1 January 2012 the GDS replaced the former ZOP, KDS and GDS.
- Recognition: gives international students access to German universities - holders of the GDS are exempt
  from the DSH/TestDaF proof of language proficiency under § 8 of the HRK/KMK Rahmenordnung (RO-DT); the
  German Länder accept it as the language proof within the teacher qualification; it is widely used as proof
  for teaching German.
blocks.telc-c1-hochschule:
telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule (the telc exam for university admission; points from the telc Handbuch "Lernziele
und Testspezifikationen", 4th edition 2015):
- A Schriftliche Prüfung (Leseverstehen, Sprachbausteine, Hörverstehen, Schriftlicher Ausdruck) taken in one
  sitting and a Mündliche Prüfung that may take place on another day. Available as a digital, hybrid or
  paper-based exam; it can also be taken as a Teilprüfung (one part only).
- Leseverstehen: 3 Teile, 90 minutes together with the Sprachbausteine. Teil 1 Textrekonstruktion (6 matching
  items, 2 points each = 12), Teil 2 selektives Verstehen (6 matching items = 12), Teil 3 Detailverstehen
  (11 richtig/falsch/nicht im Text items, 2 points each = 22) plus one Makroaufgabe on Globalverstehen
  (2 points): 48 points.
- Sprachbausteine: 1 Teil, Grammatik und Lexik, 22 four-option multiple-choice items, 1 point each = 22 points.
- Pause: 20 minutes.
- Hörverstehen: 3 Teile, about 40 minutes: Teil 1 Globalverstehen (8 matching items = 8 points), Teil 2
  Detailverstehen (10 three-option multiple-choice items, 2 points each = 20), Teil 3 Informationstransfer -
  complete 10 pieces of information, i.e. note the key points of a Vortrag (2 points each = 20): 48 points.
- Schriftlicher Ausdruck: 1 task, 70 minutes - free writing such as an Erörterung or Stellungnahme = 48 points.
- Mündlicher Ausdruck: 2 Teile, 16 minutes, usually with 2 candidates (Paarprüfung), 20 minutes of
  preparation time. Teil 1a Präsentation - choose one of two tasks and present it (6 points); Teil 1b
  Zusammenfassung/Anschlussfragen - summarise the partner's presentation, ask follow-up questions and answer
  the partner's (4 points); Teil 2 Diskussion of a quotation with Leitpunkte (6 points); plus 32 points for
  sprachliche Angemessenheit across the oral part = 48 points.
- Pass rule: at least 60 % of the points overall AND at least 60 % both in the written part (LV, HV, SA) and
  in the oral part. If only one of the two parts misses the mark, that part alone can be repeated within the
  following calendar year. The result sheet lists points and percentage per Subtest.
- Recognition: under § 8 of the HRK/KMK Rahmenordnung (RO-DT) holders of a passed "telc Deutsch C1
  Hochschule" are exempt from the DSH/TestDaF proof of language proficiency at German universities; telc
  certificates are recognised internationally by schools, universities, employers and authorities (telc is a
  full member of ALTE).
blocks.testdaf:
TestDaF (Test Deutsch als Fremdsprache, run by the TestDaF-Institut of g.a.s.t.; results on the TestDaF-Niveaus
TDN 3, TDN 4 and TDN 5, which lie on CEFR B2 to C1 - there is no pass/fail, each part gets its own TDN):
- Two formats with the same goal and the same levels: the digital TestDaF (at the computer in a g.a.s.t. test
  centre) and the paper-based TestDaF. Both have four parts - Lesen, Hören, Schreiben, Sprechen - which are
  scored separately and shown separately on the certificate; results below TDN 3 appear as "unter TDN 3".
- University admission: a TestDaF with at least TDN 4 in all four parts counts as proof of language
  proficiency for admission to all degree programmes at German universities (RO-DT § 4). Universities may
  accept a lower TDN in single parts for some subjects (e.g. TDN 3 in Schreiben for Informatik or
  Ingenieurwissenschaften) or demand TDN 5 (e.g. Übersetzungswissenschaften); TDN 5 lies above the admission
  level. Recognised by all German universities for all programmes; offered at over 500 test centres in about
  100 countries. Topics and tasks always relate to university study; no subject knowledge is required.
- Digital TestDaF - Lesen: 7 Aufgaben, 34 items, about 55 minutes (Lückentext 5 items, Textabschnitte ordnen
  4, Multiple-Choice 7, Sprachhandlungen zuordnen 4, Aussagen Kategorien zuordnen 7, Aussagen einem
  Begriffspaar zuordnen 4, Fehler in Zusammenfassung erkennen 3). Hören: 7 Aufgaben, 30 items, about 40
  minutes (typed short answers, matching, multiple choice, Laut- und Schriftbild abgleichen; audio and video
  sources). Tasks come in a fixed order, you cannot go back, and extra try-out tasks are mixed in but not
  counted.
- Digital TestDaF - Schreiben: 2 Aufgaben, about 60 minutes, typed: an argumentative text of at least 200
  words and a summary of a reading text plus a graphic of about 100-150 words. Sprechen: 7 Aufgaben, about 35
  minutes, with a fictional conversation partner over headphones and recorded answers; speaking times from
  0:45 to 2:30 minutes per task (Rat geben, Optionen abwägen, Text zusammenfassen, Informationen abgleichen
  und Stellung nehmen, Thema präsentieren, Argumente wiedergeben und Stellung nehmen, Maßnahmen kritisieren).
- Digital scoring: each part is transformed to a scale of 0-20 points (total 0-80): 0-4 = unter TDN 3,
  5-9 = TDN 3, 10-15 = TDN 4, 16-20 = TDN 5. Lesen and Hören are scored automatically (short answers by
  trained raters); Schreiben and Sprechen are rated by trained raters on whether the text refers to the
  topic, covers all points of the task, carries out the required Schreib-/Sprechhandlungen, renders the
  sources correctly in your own words, uses precise expression with varied grammar, vocabulary and
  Redemittel, and stays comprehensible despite some errors (Sprechen also: fluency, pronunciation and
  intonation).
- Paper-based TestDaF: pure exam time 3 h 15 min with breaks between the parts. Leseverstehen: 3 texts
  (Kurztexte, journalistischer Text, Text aus einer Fachzeitschrift), 30 items (10 Zuordnung, 10
  Multiple-Choice, 10 ja/nein/Text sagt dazu nichts), 60 minutes - after 50 minutes you get 10 minutes to
  transfer the answers to the Antwortblatt. Hörverstehen: 3 texts (Dialog, Interview, Vortrag/Interview),
  25 items (8 Kurzantworten, 10 richtig/falsch, 7 Kurzantworten), 40 minutes incl. 10 minutes for the
  Antwortblatt after Hörtext 3. Schriftlicher Ausdruck: 1 task, a structured handwritten text with
  Grafikbeschreibung and Argumentation, 60 minutes. Mündlicher Ausdruck: 7 tasks in typical university
  situations, 35 minutes, at the computer with headphones - there is no live examiner conversation.
- Paper-based scoring: 1 point per correct item (Lesen max 30, Hören max 25); the TDN thresholds are set per
  test version by statistical analysis - TDN 5 from 24, 25 or 26 points (Lesen) / 19, 20 or 21 (Hören),
  TDN 4 from 20-22 / 15-17, TDN 3 from 14-16 / 10-12. Each of the 7 speaking tasks is assigned to TDN 3, 4
  or 5.
- Fee and certificate validity are not stated on the official overview pages; ask the test centre for the
  current fee and the university for how old the certificate may be.
blocks.dsh:
DSH (Deutsche Sprachprüfung für den Hochschulzugang), governed by the HRK/KMK "Rahmenordnung über Deutsche
Sprachprüfungen für das Studium an deutschen Hochschulen" (RO-DT, version HRK 4 November 2025 / KMK 27 November
2025) with the DSH-Musterprüfungsordnung (DSH-MPO) as its Anlage 1:
- The DSH is run by each university or Studienkolleg under its own local Prüfungsordnung, which must follow
  the RO-DT and the DSH-MPO and is registered with the HRK in cooperation with the FaDaF. Dates, fees
  (universities may charge for the DSH), repeat rules and the concrete tasks therefore differ from university
  to university - always check the local DSH page.
- Result levels: the certificate shows the weighted overall result as DSH-1 (Eingangsstufe), DSH-2 or DSH-3
  plus the result of each Teilprüfung. DSH-1 = at least 57 % in both the written and the oral exam; DSH-2 =
  at least 67 % in both; DSH-3 = at least 82 % in both. The exam as a whole is passed when the written part
  and the oral part each reach at least 57 %. The RO-DT does not map DSH-1/2/3 to CEFR levels.
- DSH-2 is the result that counts as proof of language proficiency for admission to all degree programmes
  (RO-DT § 3 Abs. 6); a university may set DSH-1 (lower) or DSH-3 (higher) for specific programmes. An
  admission based on DSH-1 is not binding for other universities or a change of programme.
- Written exam (schriftliche Prüfung), three Teilprüfungen weighted HV : LV : WS : TP = 2 : 2 : 1 : 2 (LV and
  WS form one joint Teilprüfung). The tasks cover at least two different topic areas, none requires subject
  knowledge, and the whole written exam including the Hörtext presentation takes at most four hours.
  Monolingual paper dictionaries are allowed, nothing else. The written exam may be held as an electronic exam
  on site (elektronische Präsenzprüfung), which is equivalent to the paper version.
- Hörverstehen (HV, "Verstehen und Verarbeiten eines Hörtextes"): a lecture-style text of 5,500-7,000
  characters is presented twice (notes allowed); 10 minutes of working time after the first and 40 minutes
  after the second presentation, the presentation time itself not counted. Tasks such as answering questions,
  a Strukturskizze, a Resümee or presenting the line of thought; marked for completeness and appropriateness,
  not for linguistic correctness.
- Leseverstehen und wissenschaftssprachliche Strukturen (LV + WS): 90 minutes including reading time; a
  largely authentic, study-related text of 4,500-6,000 characters, possibly with a graphic or diagram. LV tasks
  such as questions, describing the argument structure or Gliederung, explaining passages, writing headings or
  a summary (marked for content, not language); WS tasks on the text's academic structures - completions,
  comprehension questions, paraphrase or transformation (marked for linguistic correctness).
- Vorgabenorientierte Textproduktion (TP): 70 minutes, an argumentative Sachtext of about 250 words on a
  study-related topic built from given input (diagrams, keyword lists, tables, graphics, quotations or short
  texts - Darstellen, Zusammenfassen, Vergleichen, Begründen, Bewerten, Stellung nehmen); it must not become a
  free essay. Marked for content (completeness, development, structure, coherence) and - weighted more
  heavily - language (correctness, word choice, syntax, cohesion).
- Oral exam (mündliche Prüfung): at most 20 minutes plus 20 minutes of preparation (monolingual paper
  dictionary allowed) - a Kurzvortrag of at most 5 minutes, mostly descriptive, based on a short text and/or a
  graphic, then a Gespräch of at most 15 minutes (Darstellen, Zusammenfassen, Vergleichen, Begründen,
  Bewerten, Stellung nehmen). No group exams. Assessed on content, comprehensibility and independence of the
  statements, interaction, grammatical accuracy and lexical range, pronunciation and intonation. The oral
  exam is compulsory (no exemption) and may be dropped when the written exam is failed; a university may offer
  it online as an elektronische Fernprüfung as an alternative to the on-site exam.
- Repeating the DSH is allowed; how often and when is set by the local Prüfungsordnung.
- Recognition: a DSH passed under the RO-DT and registered with the HRK is accepted by the German universities
  as proof of language proficiency (RO-DT § 7). Exempt from the DSH/TestDaF requirement are, among others,
  holders of the Goethe-Zertifikat C2: GDS, the ÖSD Zertifikat C2 and telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule (RO-DT § 8).
blocks.osd:
ÖSD (Österreichisches Sprachdiplom Deutsch) - a separate provider, not Goethe and not telc:
- A state-recognised exam system for German as a foreign and second language from Austria; since 2009 an
  independent, self-financing non-profit association; the first exams took place in 1995, today more than
  100,000 candidates a year at about 400 licensed centres worldwide. "ÖSD" also stands for Österreich -
  Schweiz - Deutschland: the standard varieties of all three countries count as equal, and the Lesen and
  Hören texts come from all three (pluricentric standard German).
- Levels: ÖSD Zertifikat A1 to C2 (ZA1-ZC2), plus youth versions and job-specific exams (e.g. ÖSD Zertifikat
  C1 Pflege und medizinische Berufe, ÖSD Zertifikat C2 Wirtschaftssprache Deutsch).
- ÖSD Zertifikat C1 (ZC1): for learners from 16 (a youth version from 14), aimed especially at people who want
  to study at a German-speaking university. Two modules, Schriftliche Prüfung (Lesen, Hören, Schreiben) and
  Mündliche Prüfung (Sprechen), taken together or separately: a Gesamtzertifikat when both are passed at one
  date or within one year at the same centre, otherwise a Modulzertifikat per module. Since 1 January 2024
  also as a digital exam.
- ZC1 parts: Lesen - 4 Aufgaben, 90 minutes (authentic texts from Austria, Germany and Switzerland, global
  and detailed understanding); Hören - 2 Aufgaben, about 40 minutes (standard-language authentic recordings,
  global, detailed and selective understanding); Schreiben - 2 texts from given input, a formal e-mail and a
  written Referat, Stellungnahme or Kommentar, 90 minutes; Sprechen - 3 Aufgaben (Telefongespräch,
  Diskussion, Kurzreferat), 15-20 minutes, conducted and rated by two trained ÖSD examiners.
- ÖSD Zertifikat C2 (ZC2): for learners from 16; four modules Lesen, Hören, Schreiben and Sprechen that can be
  taken independently at different dates (Gesamtzertifikat when all four are passed at one date or within one
  year at the same centre, otherwise a Modulzertifikat per module). Lesen - 4 Aufgaben, 90 minutes; Hören -
  3 Aufgaben, about 40 minutes; Schreiben - 2 texts from given input, 90 minutes; Sprechen - 3 Aufgaben
  (Telefongespräch, Präsentation, Diskussion on the presented topic), 15-20 minutes. Also digital since
  1 January 2024.
- Points and pass marks per module are not given on the exam pages; they follow the official Auswertungsbogen
  and Prüfungsordnung linked on osd.at.
- Recognition in Austria: for admission to a German-language degree Austrian universities require an ÖSD
  certificate between B1 and C2 depending on university and programme (and A2 already at application since
  the 2019 summer semester); ÖSD certificates from A1 upwards also serve as language proof for residence
  titles.
- Recognition in Germany: accepted by German universities at B2, C1 or C2 depending on the university; the
  ÖSD Zertifikat C2 exempts from DSH/TestDaF under § 8 of the RO-DT; the ÖSD Zertifikat B1 counts for
  naturalisation.
blocks.redemittel:
Useful Redemittel (phrases) by function:
- Planning something together (Goethe B1 Sprechen Teil 1, telc B1 Teil 3, DTZ Teil 3, Goethe A2 Teil 3):
  "Wie wäre es, wenn wir ...?", "Ich schlage vor, dass ...", "Was hältst du davon, ...?", "Sollen wir
  lieber ... oder ...?", "Das ist eine gute Idee, aber ...", "Ich würde lieber ..., weil ...",
  "Einverstanden.", "Da bin ich nicht sicher, vielleicht ...", "Könntest du dich um ... kümmern?",
  "Ich kümmere mich um ...", "Dann machen wir das so: ..."
- Presenting (Goethe B1 Teil 2): "Ich möchte euch heute etwas über das Thema ... erzählen.", "Zuerst
  spreche ich über meine eigenen Erfahrungen, dann über die Situation in meinem Heimatland, danach über
  Vor- und Nachteile, und zum Schluss sage ich meine Meinung.", "Ich persönlich habe die Erfahrung
  gemacht, dass ...", "In meinem Heimatland ist es üblich, dass ...", "Ein großer Vorteil ist ..., ein
  Nachteil ist dagegen ...", "Meiner Meinung nach ...", "Zusammenfassend kann man sagen, dass ...",
  "Vielen Dank für eure Aufmerksamkeit. Habt ihr noch Fragen?"
- Feedback and questions (Goethe B1 Teil 3): "Danke für deine Präsentation, das war sehr interessant.",
  "Besonders interessant fand ich, dass ...", "Ich habe noch eine Frage: ...", "Wie ist das bei dir
  persönlich?", "Ich sehe das ähnlich/anders, weil ..."
- Giving an opinion / arguing (Forumsbeitrag, Diskussion): "Ich bin der Meinung, dass ...", "Ich finde es
  wichtig, dass ...", "Einerseits ..., andererseits ...", "Dafür spricht, dass ...; dagegen spricht,
  dass ...", "Ein Beispiel dafür ist ...", "Ich stimme dir zu, aber ...", "Da bin ich anderer Meinung,
  weil ...", "Aus meiner Sicht ...", "Es kommt darauf an, ob ...", "Deshalb/Daher/Aus diesem Grund ..."
- Describing a picture (DTZ Teil 2A): "Auf dem Bild sehe ich ...", "Im Vordergrund/Hintergrund ...",
  "Links/Rechts ...", "Die Frau sieht ... aus.", "Ich glaube, die Leute ... gerade.", "Das Bild zeigt
  eine Situation, die ich gut kenne: ..."
- Talking about a text or statistic (telc B1 Teil 2, B2): "In meinem Text geht es um ...", "Die Grafik
  zeigt, dass ...", "Die meisten ... / Nur wenige ...", "Das überrascht mich (nicht), weil ...", "Bei
  uns ist das ähnlich/ganz anders."
- Getting to know each other (telc B1 Teil 1, DTZ Teil 1): "Darf ich fragen, woher du kommst?", "Was
  machst du beruflich?", "Wie lange lernst du schon Deutsch?", "Was machst du gern in deiner Freizeit?"
- Formal letters: "Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren,", "Ich schreibe Ihnen, weil ...", "Ich interessiere
  mich für ...", "Leider muss ich Ihnen mitteilen, dass ...", "Ich möchte mich über ... beschweren.",
  "Ich bitte Sie, ... / Könnten Sie mir bitte mitteilen, ob ...?", "Über eine schnelle Antwort würde
  ich mich sehr freuen.", "Mit freundlichen Grüßen".
- Informal letters: "Liebe Anna, / Lieber Tom,", "vielen Dank für deine Nachricht.", "Ich habe mich sehr
  gefreut, dass ...", "Wollen wir ...?", "Melde dich bald!", "Ich freue mich auf dich.", "Liebe Grüße".
- Connectors that raise the Kohärenz score: "zuerst, dann, danach, außerdem, deshalb, trotzdem,
  allerdings, zum Beispiel, einerseits ... andererseits, zum Schluss, obwohl, damit, sodass".
blocks.strategy:
Strategy and common mistakes:
- Reading: read the questions first, underline key words, work through the easy Teile first (matching ads,
  the instruction text), skip and return, and leave about 5 minutes to transfer all answers to the
  Antwortbogen - only the Antwortbogen is marked. Matching tasks: cross out ads already used; expect that
  some people get "kein passendes Angebot"/"x" and do not force a match. Opinion tasks (ja/nein): a
  comment can contain "aber" - decide by the overall stance, not by the first sentence.
- Listening: use the reading time before each part to predict the topic and the kind of information asked
  (number, place, reason). Mark answers while listening, never afterwards from memory. In parts played
  twice, use the first run for the main idea and the second for checking. Do not stop on an unknown
  word; the next item is coming. Guess rather than leave items blank (no negative marking).
- Writing: spend 2-3 minutes planning (one line per content point), write, then keep 3-5 minutes to check
  verb endings, verb position in subordinate clauses (weil/dass/obwohl send the verb to the end),
  capitalisation of nouns, "Sie/Ihnen/Ihr" capitalised in formal letters, commas before "dass/weil",
  salutation and closing. Cover EVERY content point; a missing point costs more than several small grammar
  errors. Memorised text that does not fit the task is penalised. Respect the approximate length: clearly
  too short answers lose points; going somewhat over is fine.
- Speaking: react to your partner (questions, agreement, disagreement), do not deliver a monologue in a
  dialogue task; use the preparation time for keywords, not full sentences; when you do not understand,
  ask ("Könntest du das bitte wiederholen?"). Pronunciation is rated too: speak slowly and clearly.
- Typical learner errors examiners see: wrong verb position after subordinating conjunctions, missing
  or wrong articles/adjective endings, dative/accusative after prepositions (in + Akk = direction, in +
  Dat = location), Perfekt with the wrong auxiliary, "ich bin 20 Jahre" (missing "alt"), "Ich habe
  Interesse für" (correct: "an"), mixing du/Sie, "Mit freundlichen Grüßen," with a comma, forgetting the
  subject after a fronted element (verb must stay in position 2).
- Time plan (example B1): 6-8 weeks, 45-60 minutes daily; each week one full listening set and one reading
  set from an official Modellsatz, two timed writing tasks, three speaking sessions (record yourself),
  vocabulary by topic (Arbeit, Wohnen, Gesundheit, Reisen, Medien, Umwelt, Bildung, Familie, Einkaufen,
  Freizeit, Ernährung, Verkehr, Ämter) with gender, plural and one example sentence; a full timed mock
  exam in the last week.
blocks.compare:
Choosing an exam:
- Goethe B1/B2 are modular (pass and certify module by module, repeat only a failed module); telc B1/B2
  are one exam with a written and an oral part that must both reach 60 %, but a failed part can normally be
  repeated alone within a year.
- telc has a separate Sprachbausteine part (grammar and vocabulary in gap texts); Goethe has no separate
  grammar part - grammar counts inside writing and speaking.
- Goethe B1 Sprechen contains a structured presentation with five slides; telc B1 Sprechen has a
  get-to-know-you part, a conversation about a short text or statistic, and a planning task. Both are
  pair exams.
- Goethe B1 Schreiben has three tasks (informal e-mail, opinion text, short formal message); telc B1 has
  one semi-formal/formal letter with four Leitpunkte. Goethe B2 asks for at least 150 + 100 words in two
  tasks; telc B2 asks for one letter of roughly 150 words or more with a choice between two tasks.
- The DTZ is free for integration-course participants, reports A2 or B1 per area, and is designed for
  everyday life in Germany (letters to offices, landlords, schools). It is accepted for the settlement
  permit and naturalisation like Goethe/telc B1; for university admission or professional recognition
  institutions usually ask for Goethe, telc, ÖSD or TestDaF/DSH at the required level instead.
- ÖSD (Austria) offers equivalent A1-C2 exams recognised in Germany, Austria and Switzerland; the ÖSD
  Zertifikat B1 is the same exam as the Goethe-Zertifikat B1 (jointly developed).
- Difficulty is comparable at the same CEFR level; choose by format preference (modular vs one exam,
  presentation vs statistics), availability of dates, price, and what the target institution accepts.
- Above B2, for studying in Germany (HRK/KMK Rahmenordnung RO-DT, §§ 4, 7 and 8): the DSH is set and run by
  each university and reports DSH-1/DSH-2/DSH-3 (DSH-2 is the usual admission level); the TestDaF is one
  central exam at licensed centres and reports TDN 3/4/5 per part (TDN 4 in all four parts is the usual
  admission level); the Goethe-Zertifikat C2: GDS, the ÖSD Zertifikat C2 and telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule
  exempt from the DSH/TestDaF requirement; the ÖSD Zertifikat C1 is accepted by some German universities
  (osd.at lists them) - for the Goethe-Zertifikat C1 or any other certificate check the institution's own
  list. Goethe C1/C2 and ÖSD C2 are modular; telc C1 Hochschule has a written and an oral part that must both
  reach 60 %.
blocks.grammar-perfekt:
Perfekt and Partizip II (reference):
- Perfekt = haben/sein (position 2) + Partizip II at the end: "Ich habe gestern Pizza gegessen."
- sein is used with verbs of movement from A to B (gehen, fahren, fliegen, kommen, laufen, reisen,
  fallen, steigen, aufstehen), change of state (einschlafen, aufwachen, sterben, wachsen, werden) and
  with sein, bleiben, passieren, geschehen: "Ich bin nach Hause gegangen", "Wir sind nach Berlin gefahren",
  "Sie ist eingeschlafen", "Er ist zu Hause geblieben". fahren/fliegen take haben only with a direct
  object: "Ich habe das Auto gefahren."
- All other verbs, all reflexive verbs and all modal verbs take haben: "Ich habe eine Stunde auf euch
  gewartet" (warten + haben; warten is not separable), "Ich habe mich gefreut", "Wir haben viel Spaß
  gehabt" (Spaß haben, never "Spaß spielen").
- Regular Partizip II: ge- + stem + -t (machen -> gemacht, arbeiten -> gearbeitet). Verbs ending in
  -ieren take no ge- (studieren -> studiert); inseparable prefixes be-, ver-, er-, ent-, zer-, emp-,
  miss- take no ge- (besuchen -> besucht, verkaufen -> verkauft, erklären -> erklärt).
- Irregular Partizip II you must know: gehen gegangen, kommen gekommen, fahren gefahren, fliegen
  geflogen, laufen gelaufen, bleiben geblieben, sein gewesen, werden geworden, haben gehabt, essen
  gegessen, trinken getrunken, sehen gesehen, lesen gelesen, schreiben geschrieben, sprechen gesprochen,
  nehmen genommen, geben gegeben, finden gefunden, helfen geholfen, werfen geworfen, treffen getroffen,
  beginnen begonnen, schlafen geschlafen, stehen gestanden, sitzen gesessen, liegen gelegen, tun getan,
  denken gedacht, bringen gebracht, wissen gewusst, kennen gekannt, verlieren verloren, vergessen
  vergessen, verstehen verstanden, anrufen angerufen, aufstehen aufgestanden, einladen eingeladen.
- Präteritum is used in writing and for war/hatte/modals: "Ich war müde", "Ich hatte keine Zeit",
  "Ich konnte nicht kommen". In speech the Perfekt is normal for the past.
blocks.grammar-prepositions:
Prepositions and cases (reference):
- Always Akkusativ: durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, entlang (after the noun): "für dich", "ohne den
  Schlüssel".
- Always Dativ: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu, gegenüber, ab: "mit dem Bus", "seit einem Jahr",
  "nach der Arbeit", "bei meinen Eltern" (dative plural adds -n to the noun unless it already ends in -n
  or -s).
- Wechselpräpositionen an, auf, hinter, in, neben, über, unter, vor, zwischen: Akkusativ for a direction
  (wohin?) - "Ich gehe in die Stadt", "Ich lege das Buch auf den Tisch"; Dativ for a place (wo?) -
  "Ich bin in der Stadt", "Das Buch liegt auf dem Tisch".
- Genitiv (formal): während, wegen, trotz, statt, innerhalb, außerhalb: "wegen des Wetters"; spoken
  German often uses the Dativ here ("wegen dem Wetter").
- Contractions: im (in dem), am (an dem), ins (in das), ans (an das), zum (zu dem), zur (zu der), vom
  (von dem), beim (bei dem); colloquial (speech only): aufs, fürs, ums, durchs, übers, hinters, unters,
  vors (+ das), hinterm, unterm, vorm (+ dem).
- Verbs with fixed prepositions: warten auf + Akk, sich freuen auf (future) / über (present) + Akk,
  denken an + Akk, sich interessieren für + Akk, sich kümmern um + Akk, sich ärgern über + Akk,
  teilnehmen an + Dat, sich beschäftigen mit + Dat, träumen von + Dat, Angst haben vor + Dat, sich
  verabreden mit + Dat, anfangen mit + Dat, fragen nach + Dat, sich bewerben um + Akk, sich entschuldigen
  für + Akk / bei + Dat (person).
- verlassen takes a direct object (Akkusativ), no preposition: "Sie verlässt das Haus."
- "nach Hause" (going home) and "zu Hause" (being at home) are fixed forms.
blocks.grammar-word-order:
Word order and conjunctions (reference):
- Main clause: the conjugated verb is in position 2; the subject is in position 1 or right after the
  verb: "Gestern bin ich nach Hause gegangen."
- Subordinate clauses put the conjugated verb at the END: dass, weil, obwohl, wenn, als, ob, damit,
  während, bevor, nachdem, seit(dem), bis, sodass, falls and all W-words in indirect questions:
  "Ich weiß, dass er morgen kommt." "Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin." "Er fragt, wann der Zug
  fährt." A comma always separates the clauses. If the subordinate clause comes first, the main clause
  starts with its verb: "Weil ich krank bin, bleibe ich zu Hause."
- Coordinating conjunctions und, oder, aber, denn, sondern change nothing: "Ich bleibe zu Hause, denn
  ich bin krank." (denn: verb stays in position 2; weil: verb goes to the end.)
- Adverbs used as connectors (deshalb, deswegen, darum, trotzdem, dann, danach, außerdem, sonst,
  also) take position 1 and the verb follows immediately: "Ich bin krank, deshalb bleibe ich zu Hause."
- wenn vs als vs wann vs ob: wenn = repeated or present/future events and conditions ("Wenn ich Zeit
  habe, lese ich", "Immer wenn es regnet ..."); als = one single event in the past ("Als ich 10 war,
  ..."); wann = the question word "when?" in direct and indirect questions ("Ich weiß nicht, wann er
  kommt"); ob = "whether" in indirect yes/no questions ("Ich weiß nicht, ob er kommt"). wann is never
  a conjunction meaning "while" or "before".
- Two-part: entweder ... oder, weder ... noch, nicht nur ... sondern auch, sowohl ... als auch, zwar ...
  aber, je ... desto (verb at the end after je, position 2 after desto).
- Mittelfeld order: time before manner before place (TeKaMoLo): "Ich fahre morgen mit dem Zug nach
  Berlin." Pronouns come before nouns; accusative pronoun before dative pronoun ("Ich gebe es ihm").
blocks.grammar-separable-verbs:
Separable and inseparable verbs (reference):
- Separable prefixes (stressed): an-, auf-, aus-, ein-, mit-, nach-, vor-, zu-, ab-, weg-, zurück-,
  fern-, weiter-, fest-, statt-, teil-, um- (usually), zusammen-. In a main clause (present, Präteritum,
  imperative) the prefix goes to the end: "Ich stehe um 7 Uhr auf." "Ruf mich an!" In a subordinate
  clause the verb is joined again at the end: "..., weil ich um 7 Uhr aufstehe." Partizip II puts -ge-
  between prefix and stem: aufgestanden, angerufen, eingekauft, mitgebracht. With zu: "aufzustehen".
- Inseparable prefixes (unstressed): be-, ge-, er-, ver-, zer-, ent-, emp-, miss-. They never separate
  and take no ge- in the Partizip II: verstehen - verstanden, bekommen - bekommen, erzählen - erzählt,
  besuchen - besucht, entscheiden - entschieden, empfehlen - empfohlen.
- Both possible, meaning changes: umfahren (um'fahren = drive around, inseparable; 'umfahren = knock
  down, separable), übersetzen, umstellen, durchschauen, wiederholen (inseparable: repeat).
- Not separable at all, despite looking like it: warten ("Ich habe auf euch gewartet"), studieren,
  telefonieren, funktionieren (all -ieren verbs), and simple verbs such as kaufen, machen, spielen.
blocks.grammar-adjective-endings:
Adjective endings (reference; only adjectives BEFORE a noun take endings):
- After der/die/das, dieser, jeder, jener, welcher, alle (weak endings): -e in Nominativ singular
  (der gute Mann, die gute Frau, das gute Kind) and in Akkusativ feminine/neuter (die gute Frau, das gute
  Kind); -en everywhere else: den guten Mann (Akk masc), dem guten Mann / der guten Frau / dem guten
  Kind (Dat), des guten Mannes (Gen), and all plurals (die guten Kinder, mit den guten Kindern).
  "dieser gute Mann", "mit jedem neuen Kollegen", "welches neue Auto".
- After ein/kein and possessives (mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, Ihr) (mixed endings): Nominativ
  ein guter Mann, eine gute Frau, ein gutes Kind; Akkusativ einen guten Mann, eine gute Frau, ein gutes
  Kind; Dativ einem guten Mann, einer guten Frau, einem guten Kind; Genitiv eines guten Mannes, einer
  guten Frau; plural always -en: keine guten Kinder, mit meinen guten Freunden.
- No article (strong endings): the adjective shows the article's ending: guter Wein, gute Milch, gutes
  Bier, gute Freunde; Akkusativ guten Wein; Dativ gutem Wein, guter Milch, gutem Bier, guten Freunden.
- viele, einige, wenige, mehrere, andere behave like adjectives (viele gute Freunde); alle like der.
- Adjectives after sein/werden/bleiben take no ending: "Der Mann ist gut." Comparative/superlative
  before a noun add the same endings: ein besseres Auto, die schönsten Tage. hoch -> hohe (das hohe
  Haus), dunkel -> dunkle, teuer -> teure.
blocks.grammar-modals-passive:
Modal verbs and passive (reference):
- Modals: können, müssen, dürfen, sollen, wollen, mögen (möchte) + infinitive at the END, without
  zu: "Ich kann morgen nicht kommen." "Das Fenster muss offen bleiben." Never "zu" after a modal, and
  never a Partizip II directly after a modal in the present.
- Present forms (ich/er): kann, muss, darf, soll, will, mag, möchte; plural: können, müssen, dürfen,
  sollen, wollen, mögen, möchten. Präteritum: konnte, musste, durfte, sollte, wollte, mochte.
- Perfekt of a modal with another verb uses the double infinitive: "Ich habe gehen müssen" (rare in
  speech; the Präteritum "Ich musste gehen" is normal). Alone: "Ich habe es gekonnt."
- Vorgangspassiv (process): werden + Partizip II - "Das Fenster wird geöffnet", Perfekt "Das Fenster ist
  geöffnet worden", with a modal "Das Fenster muss geöffnet werden" (modal + Partizip II + werden).
- Zustandspassiv (state, result): sein + Partizip II - "Das Fenster ist geöffnet" (= it is open).
  "Das Fenster ist zu" (colloquial: closed) / "ist offen" use adjectives, no verb form.
- Agent with von + Dat (people) or durch + Akk (means): "Der Brief wurde von ihr geschrieben."
- Alternatives to the passive: man ("Man kann das Fenster öffnen"), sich lassen ("Das lässt sich
  öffnen"), sein + zu + infinitive ("Das ist zu öffnen").
blocks.grammar-nouns-cases:
Nouns, gender and cases (reference):
- Definite articles: Nominativ der / die / das / die (pl); Akkusativ den / die / das / die; Dativ dem /
  der / dem / den (+ -n on the plural noun unless it ends in -n/-s: den Kindern, den Eltern); Genitiv des
  (+ -s/-es) / der / des (+ -s/-es) / der. Indefinite: ein / eine / ein; einen / eine / ein; einem / einer /
  einem; eines / einer / eines.
- Nominativ = subject; Akkusativ = direct object and after the Akkusativ prepositions; Dativ = indirect
  object (person who receives) and after the Dativ prepositions; verbs always with Dativ: helfen,
  danken, gefallen, gehören, antworten, folgen, gratulieren, passen, schmecken, fehlen.
- Gender hints - die: -ung, -heit, -keit, -schaft, -ion, -tät, -ie, -ei, -enz, -ur, most nouns in -e
  (die Miete, die Lampe; exceptions der Name, der Käse, das Ende); das: -chen, -lein, mostly -um,
  -ment, -ma, -tum (but der Moment, der Reichtum, der Irrtum), Ge- collectives (das Gebäude), infinitives
  as nouns (das Lernen); der: male persons, -er for persons and tools, -ling, -ismus, -or, -ant, -ist,
  days, months, seasons, weather, alcoholic drinks (der Wein, but das Bier), car brands.
- Frequently confused: der Karton (die Kartons), die Miete (rent; die Rate = instalment), das Fenster
  (die Fenster), die Tür (die Türen), der Schlüssel (die Schlüssel), das Haus (die Häuser), die
  Hausaufgabe (-n), der Termin (-e), die Stunde (-n), der Monat (-e), das Jahr (-e), die Zeit (-en), der
  Apfel (die Äpfel), das Mädchen (die Mädchen), der Junge (die Jungen), der Kollege (die Kollegen;
  n-declension: den/dem/des Kollegen), der Student (den Studenten), der Herr (den Herrn, die Herren).
- Plural patterns: -e (der Tisch - die Tische, often with umlaut), -en/-n (die Frau - die Frauen), -er
  (das Kind - die Kinder, with umlaut: das Buch - die Bücher), -s (das Auto - die Autos), no ending
  (der Lehrer - die Lehrer, with umlaut: der Apfel - die Äpfel).
blocks.grammar-numbers-time:
Numbers, clock times, dates and years (reference):
- 0 null, 1 eins, 2 zwei, 3 drei, 4 vier, 5 fünf, 6 sechs, 7 sieben, 8 acht, 9 neun, 10 zehn, 11 elf,
  12 zwölf, 13 dreizehn, 16 sechzehn, 17 siebzehn, 20 zwanzig, 30 dreißig, 60 sechzig, 70 siebzig,
  100 (ein)hundert, 1000 (ein)tausend, 1 000 000 eine Million.
- 21-99: units first, then "und", then tens, one word: 21 einundzwanzig, 32 zweiunddreißig, 94
  vierundneunzig, 860 achthundertsechzig, 1348 (ein)tausenddreihundertachtundvierzig. "eins" becomes
  "ein" inside a number (einundzwanzig, einhundert). Decimal comma: 3,5 = drei Komma fünf.
- Years: 1100-1999 in hundreds - 1987 = neunzehnhundertsiebenundachtzig, 1750 = siebzehnhundertfünfzig;
  from 2000 as normal numbers - 2000 = zweitausend, 2023 = zweitausenddreiundzwanzig (never
  "zwanzighundert..."). "im Jahr 2023" or just "2023", never "in 2023".
- Official clock time (24 h): 15:15 = fünfzehn Uhr fünfzehn, 17:00 = siebzehn Uhr, 20:30 = zwanzig Uhr
  dreißig. Everyday (12 h): 3:15 = Viertel nach drei, 3:30 = halb vier (halb + the NEXT hour: halb
  vier = 3:30, halb zwei = 1:30), 3:45 = Viertel vor vier, 3:05 = fünf nach drei, 3:50 = zehn vor vier,
  3:00 = drei Uhr. Regional (south/east): viertel vier = 3:15, dreiviertel vier = 3:45. "um" for a time
  (um drei Uhr), "gegen" for approximately, "ab" from, "bis" until, "von ... bis".
- Ordinals: 1. erste, 2. zweite, 3. dritte, 7. siebte, 8. achte, 19. neunzehnte, from 20. on -ste:
  zwanzigste, einundzwanzigste, dreißigste. Dates: "Heute ist der dritte Oktober" (Nominativ, der +
  -e), "am dritten Oktober" (Dativ, -en), written 3.10. or 3. Oktober; "Berlin, den 3. Oktober 2024" in
  letters. Months: Januar, Februar, März, April, Mai, Juni, Juli, August, September, Oktober, November,
  Dezember; "im Mai", "am Montag", "im Jahr 1999".
- Prices: 3,40 € = drei Euro vierzig; 0,99 € = neunundneunzig Cent; 1.250,75 € = eintausend
  zweihundertfünfzig Euro fünfundsiebzig (point for thousands, comma for cents).
